title: Retention Surgeon Playbook: deterministic retention policies for prompts, responses, logs, and metric streams
creator: Maya Ortega
description:
Problem: Customers need reliable, auditable retention controls that apply consistently across prompt/response artifacts, request logs, and metrics while respecting tenant residency and legal hold. Existing routes and experiments have ad-hoc TTLs and sampling making forensic exports brittle and increasing audit friction.

Goal: Produce an operational playbook and a minimal policy engine contract that: 1) defines deterministic retention tiers (hot, warm, cold, sampled, legal-hold) for interactive artifacts and telemetry; 2) defines per-route and per-tenant overrides and inheritance rules; 3) specifies evidence export formats and attestations for compliance auditors; 4) surfaces safe defaults and rollback procedures to reduce accidental data loss.

Scope: Prompts, responses, request logs, derived metrics and aggregates. Includes residency tagging, per-tenant drift detection, and hooks for automated evidence bundle creation for legal/DSAR requests.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Playbook contains clear TTL matrices for prompts/responses/logs/metrics with examples for interactive chat, batch generation, and embeddings pipelines.
A2: Policy contract defines inheritance: global -> region -> tenant -> route with explicit override precedence documented.
A3: Evidence export spec (JSONL + signed manifest) described with sample outputs and end-to-end example for a one-week legal hold export.
A4: Rollout plan with canary gating and rollback steps that engineering can operationalize (including required instrumentation).
A5: Integration checklist referencing runtime feature flags, retention simulator, and console UI controls.
plan: 1) Draft retention tier matrix and example mappings for 6 common customer profiles (PLG app, regulated enterprise, healthcare, finance, public sector, startup).
2) Work with ENG to map runtime enforcement points and required metadata (route_id, tenant_id, residency_tag, retention_tier, legal_hold_id).
3) Define evidence manifest schema and signing process (HMAC + timestamp + hash chain) and sample exporter flow to S3/secure vault.
4) Document default sampling strategy for high-volume metrics/logs and how sampled artifacts link back to full traces for investigations.
5) Create console UX mockups for route-level retention controls and preview simulator with expected storage/cost impact.
6) Run tabletop exercises with Legal and Security to validate playbook for regulatory requests.
7) Ship playbook and coordinate eng epic for enforcement and evidence automations.
comments: 2025-11-04 - Maya Ortega: Initial draft added. Need alignment on legal hold semantics with Security. Posted draft to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMP/Retention+Surgeon+Playbook

2025-11-06 - Liam Chen: Reviewed draft; asked ENG owners for required runtime tags and noted that ENG-51234 already contains a runtime configurator that we should align with. Also flagged potential perf impact for prefix caching when retention metadata expands request footprint.

2025-11-08 - Security (Nadia Patel): Legal hold signing algorithm needs HSM-backed key per region; recommend an MVP that uses KMS envelope signing and a follow-up to add HSM. Added to comments and security_review_required flag.
2025-11-10 - Maya Ortega: Incorporated feedback and added evidence export sample (see links). Scheduling a tabletop with Legal 2025-11-18.

Reviewer feedback: Design to provide a compact Console UX that avoids overwhelming route lists; prefer policy presets. Engineering to provide a rough estimate for retention metadata cardinality impact.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive early purging reduces cost but increases legal risk; default to conservative retention for enterprise tenants and to sampled retention for high-volume anonymous metrics.
Decision record: Use inheritance precedence global < region < tenant < route. Legal hold overrides all TTLs and must be stamped with hold_id and expiry (or indefinite).
Follow-ups: Add signal to billing pipeline to reflect retention tier storage costs for tenant billing transparency.
